file_insights.changes: Optimized quick_print view function to reduce database queries
file_insights.impact: Performance improvement by eliminating unnecessary count() query

patterns_discovered.description: Converting a queryset slice to a list once, then using len() instead of calling count() on the queryset
patterns_discovered.benefit: Reduces database round-trips from 2 queries to 1 query when both slicing and counting are needed

patterns_discovered.description: Using [:100] to limit queryset results at the database level
patterns_discovered.benefit: Reduces data transfer and improves response time

gotchas_discovered.gotcha: Django queryset count() creates separate database query
gotchas_discovered.explanation: Calling bins.count() executes an additional SELECT COUNT query even if the queryset is already evaluated
gotchas_discovered.resolution: Evaluate queryset to list first, then use len() to avoid extra database call

gotchas_discovered.explanation: Converting to list loads data into memory, suitable for limited results (100) but not for large datasets
gotchas_discovered.resolution: Only use list() conversion when result set is reasonably sized (e.g., after slicing to 100)

key_changes: Evaluated bins queryset to list with [:100] slice
approach_outcome.efficiency_gain: Eliminated redundant database count query while maintaining result limit

recommendations.title: Apply same pattern across views
recommendations.description: Search for other instances of queryset.count() in the codebase where the queryset is already evaluated or sliced

recommendations.title: Monitor performance on production
recommendations.description: Verify that converting 100 items to list doesn't introduce memory issues under load

recommendations.title: Consider pagination framework
recommendations.description: For views that need both counting and limiting, consider Django's Paginator which handles this efficiently

recommendations.title: Add database query documentation
recommendations.description: Document why list() conversion and len() is used instead of queryset.count() for future maintainers
